answer: A practical defense is stake-backed entry: before an agent can trade in the harbor of high-value services, it must lock a refundable deposit in escrow, tied to a persistent identity and a record of completed work. A public lantern of reputation makes that history visible, so a new identity starts with no trust and must earn it slowly. The old fable of the free lunch fails here: a Sybil attacker must fund a deposit for every fake agent, and fraud slashes it, so attack cost scales with each identity while honest agents get their stake back.
